summary.value: The Dong Tao, sometimes called the Dragon Chicken, is a rare meat breed from Dong Tao village in Khoai Chau District, Hung Yen Province, near Hanoi in northern Vietnam. Its trademark is a pair of hugely thick, scaly legs and feet on a heavy frame. The meat is a costly delicacy in Vietnam, and in the past these birds were raised only for the royal court and high officials. They are hard to breed. Hens tend to crush their own eggs under those bulky feet, so keepers usually hatch the eggs in an incubator, and the birds cope poorly with sudden shifts in temperature. Growth is slow, taking eight months to a year to reach a table weight of about 6.5 to 11 pounds, and males can top 13 pounds. It suits specialist breeders more than casual backyard keepers.
